hero.purpose: The marketing headline. One per page, display face.

display.purpose: The one number a screen is about - net worth, a budget remainder, an account balance.

body.purpose: Prose and form labels, capped at a 68ch measure.

label.purpose: The default inside controls - buttons, fields, list rows, the ledger payee.

caption.purpose: Metadata, axis labels, helper text. Set in ink-2, which still clears 7:1.

micro.purpose: The uppercase whisper label above a figure. Smallest type in the system.

shadows.name: card

shadows.name: elevated
shadows.purpose: The hover step for a filled button, and any surface briefly lifted.

shadows.name: dropdown
shadows.purpose: Menus, list boxes, the shared floating-panel treatment.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Dialogs and drawers. Re-declared opaque in dark.

motion.name: duration-fast

motion.name: duration-slow

narrative.overview:
A ledger whose every claim carries its receipt. This is a product about money being right, so the visual system is built the way a set of accounts is built: every value is measured before it is used, the measurement is written down beside it, and where a guarantee turns out to be impossible the system says so out loud and adds another channel rather than quietly hoping. `src/styles/ tokens.css` states the contrast ratio of every colour against every ground it can land on, names the dichromat separation of the positive/negative pair as low as 1.14:1, and then makes colour the *third* channel of money direction rather than the first. That refusal to overclaim is the design.

The paper is warm, not clinical. `canvas` is a bone white with yellow in it and dark is a warm charcoal, never pure black; a finance product spends its life next to a column of figures and a blue-white screen makes that column feel like a spreadsheet cell rather than a page. Against that paper there are exactly two saturated voices: a near-black `accent` that commands, and one working blue `brand` that points. `info` deliberately reuses the brand hue, because a notice with no verdict speaks in the product's own voice and a fifth hue would have put a second blue beside the first for no informational gain.

Density is high and quiet. A screen carries at most one loud thing - one primary button, one oversized numeral - and the signature composition is an 11px uppercase `micro` label sitting directly above a 40px `display` figure with nothing in between. The scale jump is deliberate and softening it with an intermediate step is what makes a dashboard read as generic. Everything else is set at `label` or `caption`, flat, on a strict 4px grid, so that the one loud thing is heard.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper (`#fbf9f5`), never clinical white; warm charcoal in dark, never pure black.
Two voices only: a near-black accent that commands and one blue that points.
Five grounds, and `surface-panel` is the one whose direction flips between themes.
Flat at rest. Shadow means a genuine second layer, plus one step of hover lift.
Every number that can change is tabular, without exception.
Colour is never the only channel, and the reason is measured rather than assumed.
Light and dark are two designed systems; a dark value computed from a light one is a defect.
The 44px hit area is a separate dimension from the visual box, and the primitive owns it.
Every token carries its measured contrast ratio as a trailing comment. One without is unfinished.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: `accent` and `brand` are the only saturated voices in the chrome. A screen gets one primary button. If a layout needs a third colour to make its hierarchy legible, the hierarchy is wrong and the palette is not.

rules.name: The Colour-Is-Third Rule
rules.body: Money direction is never encoded by colour alone, and colour is not even the first channel. Measured separation between `positive` and `negative` after Viénot-Brettel-Mollon simulation falls to 1.14:1 in light and 1.12:1 in dark - invisible. So every amount carries an explicit sign, inflow is set at a heavier weight than outflow, every intent surface carries an icon, and the product stays correct with all colour removed.

rules.name: The Series-Is-Secondary Rule
rules.body: Anything painted from the series ramp also carries a text label, a value, or a pattern. A chart whose only channel is series colour is a defect, and the primitives in `src/components/charts` are built so it cannot be expressed.

rules.name: The Measured Pair Rule
rules.body: Every colour token that can meet text carries its measured contrast ratio as a trailing comment beside its declaration, stated against every ground it can actually land on rather than a convenient one. A token added without its measurement is not finished.

rules.name: The Two Systems Rule
rules.body: Dark is designed, not derived. Its neutrals are warm charcoal, its chromatic values are lifted rather than flipped, and its shadows are re-declared opaque rather than reused. A dark value computed from a light one is a defect.

rules.name: The Three-Site Rule
rules.body: Every themed colour is declared in exactly three places: bare `:root`, then `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`, then `:root[data-theme="dark"]`. Fewer than three produces a toggle that works in one direction only.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that can change carries the `.tabular` utility (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`). No exceptions: every amount, rate, percentage, count, date figure and axis tick, in every locale. The rule is checked on the rendered element that holds the digits, never on an ancestor. This is what stops a re-rendered total shifting the row it sits in and what makes a column of money align on the decimal separator.

rules.name: The Two-Step Rule
rules.body: An 11px uppercase `micro` label sits directly above a 40px `display` numeral with nothing in between. The contrast is the signature composition; an intermediate size softens the pairing and the pairing is the point.

rules.name: The Real Minus Rule
rules.body: A negative amount is prefixed with U+2212, not a hyphen. At the size a ledger column is set in, a hyphen is a third of the width of the plus beside it and the column stops reading as a column.

rules.name: The Aligned Column Rule
rules.body: Amounts are end-aligned in every table, list and form field, with the currency symbol outside the alignment so digits line up across a workspace holding `PLN`, `EUR` and `JPY` in one view.

rules.name: The Spoken-Sentence Rule
rules.body: A money cell carries two strings: the drawing, marked `aria-hidden`, and a full sentence in an `sr-only` span built with `currencyDisplay: 'name'` - *"Expense of 20.00 Polish zlotys"*. A narrow currency symbol is announced inconsistently and a minus sign is not the same sentence as "an expense".

rules.name: The Never-Abbreviate-Money Rule
rules.body: An amount is never rendered as `1.2k` or `1,2 tys.` in a ledger, form, table cell, tooltip or export. Abbreviation is permitted only on a chart axis tick, where the full value is in the chart's data table and the point's accessible name.

rules.name: The 4px Rule
rules.body: Every dimension is a multiple of 4px and comes from a `--space-*` token. A hard-coded `padding: 13px` is a review rejection.

rules.name: The Composed-Chrome Rule
rules.body: No consumer re-derives the height of the chrome above it. Sticky regions and scroll margins compose the same named tokens, because two elements each claiming to clear the same edge is how a focused input ends up under a phone keyboard.

rules.name: The Closed-Ladder Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the product invents a `z-index`. There are eight named rungs (`base` 0, `nav` 30, `dropdown` 40, `overlay` 50, `modal` 60, `popover` 65, `tooltip` 70, `toast` 80) and `src/lib/cn.ts` registers them with tailwind-merge so an override genuinely wins instead of leaving two classes and letting stylesheet order decide.

rules.name: The Focus Reserve Rule
rules.body: Nothing may clip a focus ring. Any scroll container that could crop one reserves `--focus-reserve` of padding.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: A resting surface gets a hairline and a tone, never a shadow step. If a card needs a shadow to read as a card, its border or its ground is wrong.

rules.name: The One-Pixel Rule
rules.body: The press is `translate-y-px` and one shadow step down - never a bounce and never a scale. The control reads as pushed into the page rather than as shrinking.

rules.name: The Tone-In-Dark Rule
rules.body: In light, `surface` and `surface-raised` share white and elevation is carried by shadow. In dark they separate and tone carries it, because a shadow against charcoal reads as nothing.

rules.name: The Pill Means Pickable Rule
rules.body: `full` radius on a rectangle declares it a token you can pick up - a chip, a badge, an avatar. Never on a panel.

rules.name: The Hairline Honesty Rule
rules.body: If a box can be clicked, its border is `border-strong`. If it cannot, its border is `border-subtle`. There is no third case, and a decorative `border-strong` is a defect.

rules.name: The Pending-Not-Disabled Rule
rules.body: A submit button in flight uses React Aria's `isPending`: it stays focusable, gets `aria-disabled` rather than `disabled`, and announces politely. A `disabled` element loses focus the moment it is disabled, dumping a keyboard user at the top of the document with no announcement of why. The label stays in the DOM under the spinner marked `invisible`, so the button holds its measured width and a pending action never reflows its row.

rules.name: The Outline-Solid Rule
rules.body: `outline-solid` is load-bearing and `outline-none` must never appear beside it. In Tailwind v4 the outline utilities share one `--tw-outline-style` custom property: `outline-none` sets it to `none`, and `outline-2` then resolves against that, producing a ring two pixels wide and styled `none`. Every control built on that pair reports a focus colour and draws nothing.

rules.name: The Collapse-The-Tokens Rule
rules.body: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` sets the four duration tokens to 0.01ms rather than blanket-killing animations. A `!important` `animation: none` breaks components that wait on `animationend` - React Aria's overlays do exactly that to unmount an exiting popover - leaving a dialog that never closes. Collapsing durations removes all perceptible motion while every completion event still fires, and because they are tokens the collapse reaches animations written after the stylesheet was, including third-party CSS.

rules.name: The 44px Rule
rules.body: Every pointer target answers 44x44 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 §2.5.5 AAA). The `target-min` utility grows the *hit area* with a pseudo-element while the visual box stays on the size scale, so a 32px icon button keeps its 32px drawing and still answers a 44px tap. The hit area and the visual box are separate dimensions; conflating them produces a toolbar of 44px-tall ghost buttons with dead space between their labels. The expansion lives in the primitive, so a caller cannot forget it.

dos: **Do** record every colour token's measured contrast beside its declaration, against every ground it can land on. A token without its measurement is not finished.
**Do** declare every themed colour in all three sites (`:root`, the guarded media query, and `[data-theme="dark"]`), or the toggle will work in one direction only.
**Do** set every changeable number with the `.tabular` utility on the element holding the digits.
**Do** give every amount an explicit sign and set inflow heavier than outflow.
**Do** pair every series colour with a label, a value, or a pattern.
**Do** grow hit areas inside the primitive with `target-min`, never with padding on the caller.
**Do** write `outline-solid` explicitly and never place `outline-none` beside an outline width.
**Do** repaint disabled controls that carry their own label; reserve opacity for controls that do not.
**Do** use `isPending` rather than `disabled` for an in-flight action, and keep the label in the DOM so the control holds its width.
**Do** compose chrome geometry from the named tokens instead of re-deriving a height.
**Do** re-declare dark shadows opaquely and lift dark chromatic values rather than flipping them.
donts: **Don't** paint text in a series colour. The ramp guarantees 3:1 for graphical objects and explicitly does not guarantee 7:1.
**Don't** encode money direction, a chart series, a status or a category by colour alone.
**Don't** abbreviate money anywhere except a chart axis tick.
**Don't** render an amount from a float at any layer, including a tooltip.
**Don't** use a hyphen where a negative amount needs U+2212.
**Don't** put a shadow on a resting surface, or add a second shadow step to a card.
**Don't** fade text below 7:1 to create hierarchy - change weight, size or position instead.
**Don't** invent a `z-index`; take a rung from the closed ladder.
**Don't** hard-code a dimension off the 4px grid.
**Don't** animate a layout property, and don't ship an animation without a reduced-motion path.
**Don't** make a card interactive; wrap it in a `Button` or `Link` instead.
**Don't** let a tooltip or sticky region cover a focused control.
**Don't** claim blanket WCAG AAA conformance. `docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md` states exactly what is claimed, and this document must never contradict it.
